title: Emit Jacoco's branch coverage data to LCOV

timeline.body:
Fixes #12696.

Jacoco also has branch coverage data that wasn't used so far by Bazel.
Jacoco's branch coverage data respects Jacoco filtering, this wasn't done
by Bazel's branch coverage implementation.

I have thought about this, and I think this is not a full solution. This will only work if Jacoco filters out all branches for a single line, and it may happen that Jacoco filters out just some of them, and then Bazel will show all of them, not just those that are left after the filtering. I'll try to find a better solution.

timeline.body: Updated to an implementation that uses Jacoco's branch coverage data, instead of simply checking in Jacoco's source coverage whether a line was filtered or not. If this is a good direction I can try fixing the tests.
This puts all "covered" branches before all "uncovered" branches. Two executions that cause different branches to be run could not be meaningfully merged.

I believe one of the original purposes for using BranchCoverageDetail is to attempt to preserve the order of branches by examining the probes in Jacoco's [RuntimeData](https://www.jacoco.org/jacoco/trunk/doc/api/org/jacoco/core/runtime/RuntimeData.html).

The change in this PR would mean we would lose the ordering of branches, which means we could no longer merge branch coverage reports.

I don't think this can be accepted at the moment. I don't fully understand what is going on or how the branch probing works, and will have to do some investigations myself.

There are some constraints from our internal tooling that require merging of branch information to at least "mostly" work.

> I don't think this can be accepted at the moment. I don't fully understand what is going on or how the branch probing works, and will have to do some investigations myself.
> 
> There are some constraints from our internal tooling that require merging of branch information to at least "mostly" work.

Sure! First and foremost the purpose of this PR was to show how Jacoco's filtering for branches could be used by Bazel. I was also wondering about the branch ordering (yes indeed it's lost), for my case it's not an issue.
If ordering is crucial, then I guess the proper fix would be to somehow apply Jacoco's filtering in BranchCoverageDetail (I don't yet know how to do that).
